title: Flask Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Reply with text
entries.summary: A route decorator connects GET / to a function. Its return value becomes the reply.
notes: Keep the decorator directly above the function it belongs to.

entries.name: Reply with JSON
entries.summary: jsonify turns data into a JSON response. Open GET /book.
notes: JSON field order is not meaningful; Flask may sort keys.

entries.name: Read a name from a path
entries.summary: Angle brackets mark a path input. GET /hello/Ravi passes Ravi to the function.
notes: A path value is untrusted input; do not paste it into raw HTML.

entries.name: Check a path number
entries.summary: The int converter accepts a whole-number path value. Open GET /double/4.
notes: A route converter decides whether the route matches before the function runs.

entries.name: Read a query value
entries.summary: request.args reads query-string values. Open GET /search?q=cat.
notes: Query values are text unless you convert them.

entries.name: Read a JSON request
entries.summary: Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. The code checks that the body is an object with text title.
notes: Check parsed data before indexing into it.

entries.name: Report a missing item
entries.summary: Returning a response with 404 tells the client that this book was not found. Open GET /missing.
notes: A failure should not pretend to be a successful 200 response.

entries.name: Follow a named route
entries.summary: url_for builds a URL from a function endpoint name. GET /start redirects a browser to /hello.
notes: The endpoint name here is the Python function name, not the URL text.

entries.name: Add a response header
entries.summary: make_response lets you add metadata before sending a reply. GET /note has Cache-Control: no-store.
notes: Headers describe the response; changing one does not change its body.

entries.name: Run a shared check
entries.summary: before_request runs before route handlers. This practice check rejects paths under /closed. Visit GET /closed/books.
notes: Returning a response stops the request from reaching its view.

entries.name: Give a friendly error page
entries.summary: An error handler formats a known error. GET /missing uses abort to raise a 404.
notes: Keep the error status when returning a friendly error body.

entries.name: Test a request in Python
entries.summary: The test client calls the app without an open port. This example prints the returned JSON score.
notes: Use the test client only for tests; it is not a public server.
